newsitem.title: USA: CBO's O'Neill sees U.S. debt limit reached 1998.
newsitem.headline: CBO's O'Neill sees U.S. debt limit reached 1998.

text.p: U.S. Congressional Budget Office director June O'Neill said Tuesday the government's debt limit of $5.5 trillion will fund government borrowing through early 1998, a few months longer than Congress had expected when the limit was raised in March 1996.

CBO's report to the Senate Budget Committee forecast federal debt at the end of fiscal 1997 at $5.392 trillion, rising to $5.643 trillion at the end of fiscal 1998 and to $7.090 trillion at end of fiscal 2002. These forecasts assume current spending and tax policies continue with no action by Congress or the White House to reduce the budget deficit.

The lower-than-expected deficit in fiscal 1996 and the smaller projected deficit for fiscal 1997 led to lower government borrowing projections. The 1996 deficit turned out to be $107 billion, not the $144 billion projected last year and the 1997 fiscal year's deficit is now seen at $124 billion, down from the $171 billion projected by CBO last May.
Republican congressional leaders and President Clinton have said they intend to negotiate changes in spending and taxes necessary to balance the budget by 2002.

The share of debt held by the public totaled $3.733 trillion in 1996 and is expected to reach $3.869 trillion at the end of fiscal 1997, rising to $4.74 trillion at the end of fiscal 2002, the CBO reported.

CBO's report projected net interest on the public debt, the amount paid to people and institutions outside the federal government who hold federal securities, will grow from $241 billion in 1996 to $248 billion expected in fiscal 1997 and rising to $279 billion in fiscal 2002.
Debt held by the public was 49.9 percent of the total U.S. Gross Domestic Product in fiscal 1996 and would fall to 47.9 percent of GDP by 2002, the report said.
